[PATH:literature] Meta-analysis of published studies on nutrient spiraling and transient storage in intermittent streams, focusing on the relationship between network fragmentation (disjoint cycles) and nutrient retention metrics — Synthesizes existing empirical evidence across different temperate forest stream networks to evaluate the generalizability of the hypothesis that disjoint cycles deplete local nutrient retention.

[PATH:theoretical] Computational ecosystem model simulating nutrient dynamics in a network with tunable connectivity, parameterized for temperate forest streams, to compare retention outcomes under scenarios with multiple disjoint cycles versus a single connected network — Provides a controlled, reproducible test of the causal mechanism by isolating the effect of network topology on nutrient depletion, while accounting for dry-season conditions.
